exercise.name: Barbell Hang Snatch

reference.title: Barbell Hang Snatch

reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.bodyPart: Full body (hips, thighs, upper back, shoulders)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace standing tall, hold through the dip, jump and catch; breathe out once standing with the bar fixed overhead.
breathing.cadence: Dip about 0.7 s, jump and catch about 0.6 s

prescription.frequency: 1-3 times a week, early in the session
prescription.tempo: Controlled dip, explosive jump, fast drop under
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: technique-limited, every rep fast (NSCA guidance for power exercises).
prescription.progression: Add load in small steps once the overhead squat catch is stable.

cues.text: Stand tall with a wide snatch grip, bar in the hip crease, arms long.
Push the hips back and slide the bar down the thighs to just above the knees; shoulders over the bar, back flat.
Jump and shrug, pull the elbows high and out, then pull yourself down under the bar and catch it on locked arms in a deep squat.
Stand up from the squat with the bar locked overhead.
Lower the bar to the hips under control and stand tall for the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Bar swinging away from the body
mistakes.fix: Keep the bar close; brush the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Catching high and riding the bar down with bent arms
mistakes.fix: Pull under fast and lock the elbows on the way down.

mistakes.mistake: Heels lifting or chest dropping in the squat
mistakes.fix: Sit straight down with the chest up and the bar over the mid-foot.
Arms long until the hips have finished the jump.

kinematics.setup: Standing tall, bar at the top of the thighs, arms long
kinematics.peak: Hang just above the knees: knees ≈18°, trunk ≈32°
kinematics.norm: Hang just above the knees: shoulders over the bar, back flat (clinical opinion; NSCA hang variations)

kinematics.setup: Full extension on the balls of the feet, shrug, elbows high and out
kinematics.peak: Squat, knees ≈105°, arms locked overhead (elbows ≈9°); standing: upper arm ≈146° from the trunk line, bar -3.5 cm from mid-foot
kinematics.norm: Squat catch overhead on locked arms; hang variations change the power profile (Suchomel 2014, on cleans)

kinematics.setup: Wide snatch grip, 90 cm between the handle centres
kinematics.norm: Wide snatch grip, bar in the hip crease when standing (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Jump and catch 0.7 s, stand 1.2 s, down 1.6 s
kinematics.norm: Controlled dip, explosive second pull (clinical opinion)

cautions: Learn the snatch with a dowel or empty bar under coaching; use bumper plates and a clear platform.
Know how to miss: push the bar away and step out from under it.
Shoulder pain overhead or poor overhead mobility: use high pulls instead.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Hang power snatch: catch in a quarter squat.
Ankles or hips limit the squat: catch higher.

muscleNotes.triceps_l: Lock the elbows as you punch under the bar.
